svg.title: DBRuleSwitch behavioral paradigm
svg.desc: Paper-style summary figure showing protocol progression, block-switch cycle, and single-trial state structure for DBRuleSwitch.ino.

g.title: Layer 1

g.text: Increasing self-initiation period with high free-drop probability
Easy-side criterion = last 50 easy trials on each side, performance >= 75%
If the first switch goes to P9, the order becomes P5 -> P9 -> P7 -> P5.

1. Entry from P10 requires 500 valid trials and side easy performance criterion on both sides.
1. 从 P10 开始需要 500 次有效试验，并且双方都符合侧面易度标准。
2. Each block switch request is stored in PendingProtocolIndex and is not applied immediately.
3. The new protocol becomes active only at the next TrialBlockOnset (or manual switch).
4. During BlockSwitchMode, the next block starts only after InterBlockInterval, ready cue, and self-initiation.
the first 50 correct trials after a rule change receive an extra cue and reward up to 2x (capped at 200 ms).
BlockSwitchMode uses the full 5-level frequency set and congruency antibias based on PreviousRule versus current rule.
First trial of each block: TrialBlockDelay -> NeuralReader -> CapReinit -> TrialStart. Within-block trials start directly from TrialBlockDelay -> TrialStart.
Time alignment pulse is emitted at TrialStart; free drop is optional and depends on protocol stage, block onset, and error-history reward flags.
Wrong licks during shaping are ignored or loop within SampleCue.
No response goes directly to TrialEnd.
No response goes directly to TrialEnd.
Rules: rule 0 = location; rule 1 = frequency; rule 2 = reversed frequency. Valid trials for protocol progression include correct and error, but not no-response or early-lick trials.
